correctness.rationale: For an incidence graph of any existing finite projective plane, same-side distances equal two, incident opposite-side distance one and nonincident distance three. Every mixed Rips clique has at most one vertex from one bipartition side unless it is solely incidence-adjacent; therefore U is the full point simplex plus cones from individual line vertices, V the dual, each collapses to its large simplex, and U∩V equals exactly the incidence graph G. Mayer–Vietoris gives H2(K;Z)≅H1(G;Z), rank |E|−|V|+1=(q+1)(q²+q+1)−2(q²+q+1)+1=q³, and all other reduced homology zero. The order-sensitive inclusion (c,-c) in C*(U)⊕C*(V) changes sign under class-exchanging graph automorphisms; hence the integral duality-character twist (not merely rational). Exact graph chain trace: class-preservers χ=f_E−f_V+1; exchangers χ=a_E−1. Independently constructed all 168 invertible binary 3×3 maps and 168 polarities for the Fano incidence graph, and recovered the two claimed trace distributions {8:1,1:48,0:63,-1:56} and {2:28,0:84,-1:56}; weighted squared character norm is (168+168)/336=1, hence absolute irreducibility. Read actual integral fundamental-cycle checker: its eight-by-eight twisted polarity involution has trace 2 and rank_F2(T−I)=3; standard integral C2-lattice classification implies exactly Z²⊕Z[C2]³. Thus the general theorem is proved by the axioms, not an extrapolation from q=2.
residual_risks: Finite enumeration only establishes Fano specialization, not general q. The exact integer polarity matrix was checked through inspected source code and its rank assertions rather than a separate Smith-normal-form implementation. Integral C2-lattice classification is a needed classical input.

value.rationale: The incidence graph is a canonical object of every finite projective plane, and its natural full automorphism group includes correlations that interchange points and lines. The known H2 rank q³ does not say how these symmetries act integrally. The general twist and fixed-flag character, plus the absolutely irreducible eight-dimensional Fano module with three integral regular C2 blocks, give a useful structural equivariant invariant and exact lattice data unavailable from ordinary homotopy. It is a motivated uniform family theorem with a natural finite specialization, not a gratuitous q=2 instance.
residual_risks: No assumption finite planes exist for all q, no classification of every integral subgroup restriction or Borel-equivariant homology.

limitations: q=2 numerical evidence cannot prove arbitrary projective orders; general statement follows from axioms/Mayer–Vietoris.
